title_1: The world has its first trillionaire.
act_intro_3: I'm the poorest man in this world.
act_intro_4: I'm the richest man in this world.

act_merit_debate_3: I am the richest man in this world.
act_merit_debate_4: I am the poorest man in this world.
act_merit_debate_8: I have a PhD in physics.
act_merit_debate_9: If you’re so smart, / why aren’t you rich?
act_merit_debate_10: That is the tyranny of math.
fair_game_1: Let's play a game. / An experiment.
fair_game_2: I like a good experiment. / What is the rule?
fair_game_4: I knew it! / You snarky little communist! / You want to take my money.
fair_game_5: Chill out! / You will have your money back!
fair_game_6: Fine. Give him some of my coins.
fair_game_10: Tempting. But give him one back.
round1_1: We each put half on the table.
round1_4: Red side, I win. / Blue side, you win.
round2_1: Wait! / I have 4. / I can't put in as much as you.
round2_2: Put in half of what you have.
round2_5: So we always put in half of what the poorer one has?
round2_6: Yes. / That way everybody can keep playing.
round2_7: Smart. / Okay, let's go. / I'll win it back.
dare_1: Back where I started. / Well, I'm a bit ahead. / Naturally.
dare_4: Nobody has an edge. / Same odds, same rule. / Nobody gets rich.
dare_8: That being rich means nothing. / No talent, no hard work. Just luck.
dare_12: I'll bet half my wealth you can't.
dare_14: You're either very foolish, / or very poor.
dare_16: We need more players. / And many more rounds.
room_1: Different colours. / Different shapes. / Only the size counts.
rule_1: Each time, / two people are picked at random.
rule_2: They bet a tenth of what the poorer one has.
rule_3: Flip. / The winner takes it all.
offer_1: Real life is / much more complicated than this.
offer_2: Of course it is. / Want to hear a joke?
joke_1: A farmer's cow stopped giving milk. / He asked three scientists for help.
joke_2: The biologist explained how cows evolved.
joke_3: The chemist explained the chemistry of milk.
joke_4: Then it was the physicist's turn.
joke_11: It's round, like a ball. / Can you play football with it?
joke_13: And this game is my spherical cow. / Simple, but enough for our question.
joke_14: Even this fair game piles the money up. / Fair odds alone don't keep the room open.
guess_1: Now it's your turn to guess.
guess_3: What do you think will happen?
guess_3_choice_3: A split: some rich, some poor
guess_3_choice_4: One giant, the rest near nothing
guess_4: And how much would you bet on that?
guess_5: A coffee. Careful with your money. / I respect that.
guess_6: A lunch. / Fair. / The winner picks the place.
guess_8: One percent?! / Careful. / That's how it starts.
run_1: Here we go. / Fair trades, one after another.
log_run: After {trades} trades, one of them holds {share} of everything.
run_8: Run it again and see if your talent comes along.
run_9: Look at that. Am I a genius now?
why_2: The paper found the reason after the result. / The coin never saw a thing.
why_4: Let's see how that reason holds.
why_5: One run shows. It doesn't prove. / An experiment must be repeatable: / the same rule, again and again.
sort_1: A hundred people. / Too many to read at a glance.
sort_2: Most have almost nothing. A few have a lot. / That's just real life.
ruler_1: This chart is useless, though. / Everyone is squeezed into one corner.
ruler_3: Now each step means ten times more, / not ten more.
ruler_4: One, ten, a hundred, a thousand. / Even steps. Huh.
ruler_5: Less than a cent goes in the dust box. / Zero has no place on this ruler.
ruler_7: And where they started, on this ruler.
gini_1: Economists love a single number. / What's ours?
gini_2: Let's start where they started, / everyone equal.
gini_4: Now walk along the line / and add up their money as you go.
gini_5: Everyone the same: / the total climbs a straight line.
gini_7: Let the room play a while.
gini_9: The gap between them is the Gini. / Zero: all the same. One: a single owner.
gini_11: And on, to where the room is now.
gini_13: Want to see the equal case / and play with it?
count_2: A hundred players. / That's a lot of competition.
count_3: If all hundred had the same, / all hundred would count.
count_4: Take one person's money away. / No money, and you don't count. {count} left.
count_5: Half of them own it all, equally? / {count}.
count_7: Each one has half of what the one before has? / About {count}.
count_9: Your turn: four people, eight coins. / Drag a coin from one to another.
four_hint_1: Hint: give two of them everything.
turnover_1: At least it's a busy economy. / {trades} trades!
turnover_2: Count the money that actually changes hands.
turnover_3: At first, {early} of the room changed hands every round.
turnover_4: By the end, {late}. / The trades go on. The money barely moves.
turnover_5: A dead economy. / Even I don't like that.
end_1: That was one run. / It shows. It doesn't prove.
end_2: The math says more. / Keep playing forever, and one person ends up with everything.
end_4: Never on a date. It's a limit. / At any moment, it can still wobble.
end_5: Want to see it run longer?
dial_1: Your turn. / Pick a stake, from nothing to everything.
dial_2: Zero: nothing moves. / That's no game at all.
dial_4: {stake}: the stake you watched. / The richest holds {share}.
dial_6: Everything on the table: / one loss and you're out. The richest holds {share}.
dial_7: Every stake above zero ends the same way. / The stake changes the journey, not the end.
dial_8: How much longer does a smaller stake take? / Three rooms: 20%, 10%, 5%.
dial_9: The smaller the stake, / the slower they stop counting.
dial_10: Now count the time in stake squared.
dial_11: Nearly one curve. / Half the stake, about four times the trades.
stop_1: Enough watching. / Now you tax them.
stop_3: A quarter of it came out, / and everyone got an equal part.
stop_still_1: Now make the room more equal: / more than {target} players.
stop_still_2: {count} players count now. / Your hand did that.
stop_live_1: Now they trade again. / Keep more than {target} players, as long as you can.
stop_live_2: Thirty seconds, and still {count} players. / Your hand did it.
stop_live_3: It closed after {seconds} seconds. / {taps} taps weren't enough.
stop_live_4: Notice what your hand did: / watch, pick one, react. Again and again.
stop_live_5: Next, not a hand. A rule. / Nobody gets picked.
levy_1: Your hand gets tired. / A rule doesn't.
levy_2: Once a round, everyone pays the same share: / a quarter of what they hold.
levy_3: Everyone lost a quarter. / Nothing changed.
levy_4: Right. Everyone shrank the same. / The shares didn't move.
levy_5: It all goes into one pool.
levy_6: The pool is divided into equal parts, / one for each.
levy_9: The average broke even. / Below it, more came back. Above it, less.
levy_11: And the room kept every coin.
match_1: Now let it trade. Same luck, twice: / one room without the rule, one with it.
match_2: Without the rule: about {a} players. / With it: about {b}.
match_4: Every toss the same. / Only the rule changed.
match_5: Look at who holds how much.
match_6: The Gini: {giniA} without the rule, {giniB} with it.
match_7: And the money keeps moving: / {turnA} of it changes hands each round without, {turnB} with.
match_9: A small tax, every round. / Small enough to miss, big enough to keep the game open.
dials_1: Now both dials are yours: / the stake, and the tax.
dials_2: No tax, the stake you know: / about {count} players.
dials_3: The same stake, a 0.3% tax: / about {count} players.
dials_4: Double the stake, the same tax: / about {count}.
dials_5: Double the stake, four times the tax: / about {count} again.
dials_7: And every other pair? / Too many to try, one by one.
map_1: So try them all: stake across, tax up. / Each square, how many still count.
map_2: A small tax can hold a big stake: / double the stake, about four times the tax.
map_3: Too small a stake, and the money barely moves. / Too big, and the room empties fast.
map_4: Too big a tax is no better: / take every win back, and neither luck nor merit pays.
map_5: In between, the game stays open. / People still win and lose, and everyone can still play.
sandbox_2: The machine is yours. Break our argument.
bet_1: So. You bet half your wealth I couldn't prove it.
bet_2: And you didn't. You said so yourself: / one run shows, it doesn't prove.
bet_4: My lawyers will want to read the math. / And my money is tied up in the room.
bet_5: He'll find a way. / They always do.
bet_6: You called it: one giant. / Collect your bet from Blue. Good luck.
bet_7: You guessed roughly equal. / The room went the other way.
bet_8: You guessed a gentle spread. / The room went much further.
bet_9: You guessed a split. / Close. The split kept going.
bet_10: Fine. If not merit, then what?
bet_11: The coin was fair. It never saw a name.
bet_12: Money didn't buy better odds. / It bought more tosses you could survive.
bet_13: So we take it all and share it out?
limits_4: And nobody lives in either. They're the two limits.
veil_1: You're going to live under the rule you choose.
veil_2: But you don't get to choose who you'll be.
veil_3: Pick the rule before you know your fortune.
veil_4: What would you call fair, before you knew where you'd end up?

human_1: I am not going to explain how he got rich.

card_limit_2: A limit, not a date. At any moment the room can still wobble.
card_participants_1: How many equal fortunes would be just as concentrated as this room.
card_participants_2: Everyone equal: all of them. One owner: 1. No money: you don't count.

sandbox_map_title_toggle: Click or press Enter to switch all three charts between participation and Gini.
sandbox_map_tax_scale_toggle: Switch both tax axes between square-root and linear spacing.
sandbox_map_stake_scale_toggle: Switch both stake axes between ordinary and squared spacing.
sandbox_map_reference: Colors show a 100-person reference: {runs} finished runs at each interior setting. Blue means fewer effective participants; red means more, using the room's circle colors. Participation is scaled between one owner (0%) and an equal room (100%). In Gini view, red means lower Gini and blue means higher Gini. Gini keeps its usual scale: equality is 0; one owner in a two-person room gives 0.5. The same guide stays visible at every room size, although small rooms can differ. The left and bottom edges use exact limits. Tax runs from 0 to 50%. Click either axis to change its spacing; click the map to set both dials.
sandbox_map_local_description: Each outlined dot is a finished run: stake across, tax from 0 to 50% on the selected vertical scale. Color shows measured {metric}. Click to set both dials.
sandbox_map_choose: Click to set stake and tax. Press Enter to set both to 50%.
sandbox_map_aria_reference: Outcome map with {reference} settings from a 100-person reference. Blue marks fewer effective participants, red more. Participation is scaled between one owner and an equal room; Gini keeps its usual value. The current room has {people} people; its live reading is shown at the dials. Tax spans 0 to 50 percent. Your dials sit at {stake} stake and {levy} tax; dashed lines mark the cross-sections. Click an axis to change its spacing.
sandbox_map_aria_local: Outcome map of {local} measured {metric} settings for rooms of {people}. Tax spans 0 to 50 percent on the selected vertical scale, with ticks labeled in actual percentages. Your dials sit at {stake} stake and {levy} tax; dashed lines mark the cross-sections when in range.
sandbox_map_colorbar_participants: Participation color scale: blue at the bottom is one effective participant; red at the top is an equal room.
sandbox_map_colorbar_gini: Gini color scale: blue at the bottom is high inequality; red at the top is equality.
sandbox_curve_tax_description: A cut through the 100-person reference at one stake. {metric} runs across; tax runs up from 0 to 50% on the same scale as the map. Hover the map to preview another stake. Local participation points use this room's own limits.
sandbox_curve_tax_local_description: A cut through your finished runs at one stake. {metric} runs across; tax runs up on the same selected scale as the map. Hover the map to preview another stake.
sandbox_curve_tax_aria: Tax versus {metric} at stake {stake}. Tax runs vertically from 0 to 50 percent on the same scale as the outcome map. Click the tax axis to switch its scale; click the horizontal axis to toggle its scale.
sandbox_curve_stake_description: A cut through the 100-person reference: {metric} against stake, with tax held fixed. Zero stake stays equal; at zero tax, every positive stake uses the one-owner limit. Local participation points use this room's own limits. Hover the map to preview another tax.
sandbox_curve_stake_scale_note: Stake positions are squared; click the stake axis to return to even spacing.
sandbox_curve_stake_aria: {metric} against stake at tax {levy}, cut through the reference outcomes. The left edge and zero-tax limit are exact; other points average finite runs. Click an axis to toggle its scale.
sandbox_room_aria: A sandbox room of {count} agents trading under your rules. Click a person to tax them; Shift and click gives them the room's tax. Ctrl and click photographs them for The Morning Ledger; Ctrl, Shift, and click photographs them for The People's Gazette.
sandbox_room_shortcuts: Click: tax · Shift+click: give · Ctrl+click: Morning Ledger · Ctrl+Shift+click: People's Gazette
sandbox_hist_description: The wealth distribution: each bar counts the people whose holdings fall in that range. Hover for median and mean.
sandbox_hist_title_toggle: {count} bins. Click or press Enter for the next bin count.
sandbox_hist_aria: Wealth histogram, {count} {xscale} bins, {yscale} people axis. Click an axis to toggle its scale; click the title to change the bin count.
sandbox_time_description_inequality: How concentrated the room is over time: Gini (solid) and the biggest holding (dashed). Click the title for the next view.
sandbox_time_description_agents: Ten tracked people, each line one personal fortune — a multiplicative random walk. Click the title for the next view.
sandbox_time_description_volume: Dollars traded per round. The strong line is smoothed with a trailing four-round half-life; the faint line behind it shows raw turnover. Click the title for the next view.
sandbox_time_title_toggle: Click or press Enter for the next time view.
sandbox_time_aria: {title} over {rounds} rounds, anchored at round one. Click the title for the next view, or an axis to toggle its scale.
stop_over_won: You kept {count} players for thirty seconds.
veil_message: I chose a {levy} tax. What would you call fair, before you knew where you'd end up?
veil_strip: Someone chose this world for you: a {levy} tax. Read on, and choose yours.
